fact: 1911年9月28日，意大利政府以其在的黎波里塔尼亚与昔兰尼加的利益受侵害为借口，向奥斯曼政府发出限24小时答复的最后通牒；奥斯曼方面于29日提出谈判，意方拒绝，当日宣战。战争在摩洛哥危机之后爆发，意方判断列强不会干预。

sources.title: Italo-Turkish War 1911-1912（1914-1918 Online: International Encyclopedia of the First World War，Rachel Simon）
sources.quote: An Italian ultimatum reached the Ottoman government on 28 September 1911, to be accepted within twenty-four hours. It stated Italy's decision to expand her authority over Libya, otherwise she threatened to use force. The Ottomans responded on 29 September trying to negotiate, which was unacceptable to the Italians, who declared war later that day.

sources.title: Italo-Turkish War（Encyclopaedia Britannica）
sources.quote: Using the pretext of the infringement of Italian interests in the two provinces, the Italian government issued an ultimatum to Turkey on Sept. 28, 1911, and on the next day declared war.

fact: 1911年10月1日，约44500人的意大利远征军抵达利比亚海岸；10月2日要求驻的黎波里的奥斯曼军队投降，3日炮击该城，4日登陆时未遇抵抗。奥斯曼驻军仅约5000名步兵与350名骑兵，指挥部判断力量悬殊，主动退往内地组织抵抗。

sources.title: Italo-Turkish War 1911-1912（1914-1918 Online，Rachel Simon）
sources.quote: The occupying force (numbering some 44,500 troops) reached the Libyan coast on 1 October 1911. Italy called on the Ottomans in Tripoli to surrender on 2 October 1911 and bombarded Tripoli the following day. ... Consequently, when on 4 October 1911 the Italians landed in Tripoli, they faced no resistance.

sources.title: Italo-Turkish War（Encyclopaedia Britannica）
sources.quote: Italian forces quickly occupied the towns of Tripoli, Darnah (Derna), and Banghāzī (Benghazi), but unexpected resistance on the part of the Muslim population forced the Italian commander General Carlo Caneva to confine operations to the coastal areas.

fact: 1911年10月23日与26日，抵抗力量在的黎波里郊外袭击意军，打死数百人；进攻被击退后，意军对当地居民实施报复，杀害4000余人。这次镇压打消了意大利国内认为占领会轻易完成的判断，也使抵抗更坚决。

sources.title: Italo-Turkish War 1911-1912（1914-1918 Online，Rachel Simon）
sources.quote: On 23 and 26 October 1911, in the outskirts of Tripoli, the resistance attacked Italian troops killing several hundred. The attackers were repelled and Italy severely punished the indigenous population, killing over 4,000.

fact: 1911年11月5日，意大利颁布敕令宣布吞并的黎波里；1912年2月23日意大利议会通过批准吞并的法案。战争并未因此结束，直到1912年10月18日《乌希条约》（亦称第一次《洛桑条约》）签订，奥斯曼才把对的黎波里与昔兰尼加的权利让与意大利；意大利承诺撤出佐泽卡尼索斯群岛，实际继续占领。

sources.title: Page:Statesman's Year-Book 1913.djvu/1127（Wikisource）
sources.quote: On November 5, 1911, a decree was issued annexing Tripoli, and on February 23, 1912, the Italian Chamber passed the Bill which ratified the decree of annexation. ... continued until October 18, 1912, when the Treaty of Ouchy was signed, by which the Sovereignty of Italy in Tripoli was established.

sources.title: Italo-Turkish War（Encyclopaedia Britannica）
sources.quote: By the terms of the Treaty of Lausanne (also called Treaty of Ouchy; Oct. 18, 1912), Turkey conceded its rights over Tripoli and Cyrenaica to Italy. Although Italy agreed to evacuate the Dodecanese, its forces continued to occupy the islands.

fact: 1911年10月23日，意大利陆军航空队上尉皮亚扎驾驶一架布莱里奥XI型单翼机，在的黎波里与阿齐齐亚之间的奥斯曼阵地上空进行约一小时的侦察飞行，这是飞机首次用于战争。九天后（11月1日），加沃蒂少尉驾驶鸽式（Etrich Taube）飞机在塔吉拉绿洲与艾因扎拉一带向土军阵地投下4颗各约2千克的榴弹，为世界首次空中轰炸。

sources.title: Air force（Encyclopaedia Britannica）
sources.quote: The first use of an airplane in war was on October 23, 1911, during the Italo-Turkish War, when an Italian pilot made a one-hour reconnaissance flight over enemy positions near Tripoli, Libya, in a Blériot XI monoplane. The first bombing raid came nine days later, when a pilot dropped four grenades on Turkish positions.

sources.title: 空袭的产生与发展是怎么样的？（福建省人民政府）
sources.quote: 1911年10月23日,意大利飞行员皮亚扎上尉驾驶一架“布莱里奥”飞机飞往的黎波里与阿齐齐亚之间的土耳其阵地上空进行侦察。11月1日,意大利飞行员朱里奥·加沃蒂少尉驾驶“鸽”式飞机,在北非塔吉拉绿洲和艾因扎拉地区向土军阵地投下了4颗各重2千克的“西佩利”式榴弹。这是世界飞机作战史上的第一次空袭。

fact: 的黎波里一带的esparto草（alfā）由人工手采，一个劳力的日采集量为2至3英担（约100至150公斤）；叶片在干燥的夏季采集，此时叶片与茎的附着较松，其他季节强行剥离往往会连根拔起。这是当地农村最主要的现金收入来源之一。

sources.title: 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica/Esparto（Wikisource）
sources.quote: The leaves are gathered by hand, and from 2 to 3 cwt. may be collected in a day by a single labourer. They are generally obtained during the dry summer months, as at other times their adherence to the stems is so firm as often to cause the uprooting of the plants in the attempt to remove them.

fact: 大麦是当地平民的主食，小麦种植在19世纪末已大量被大麦取代；由于小麦与大麦连年歉收，自1881年开始进口外国面粉，且规模不断扩大。这意味着当地口粮依赖海运输入，一旦港口被封锁或战区扩大，面包供应立即受制于外部。

sources.title: 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica/Tripoli (North Africa)（Wikisource）
sources.quote: The cultivation of wheat was largely supplanted by that of barley—the staple food of the peasantry, whilst esparto grass, a fibre growing wild in the rural districts within the cereal zone, acquired the chief place among local exports. The importation of foreign flour, begun in 1881, assumed large dimensions in providing for the deficiencies occasioned by ever-recurring failures of the wheat and barley harvests.

sources.title: Page:Statesman's Year-Book 1913.djvu/1127（Wikisource）
sources.quote: Barley is the chief food of the people. Cultivation in Tripolitania does not amount to much, though cotton, tobacco, castor beans, saffron, indicus, and henna are grown.

fact: 青年土耳其革命后，利比亚的阿拉伯人与犹太人一直保持免服奥斯曼兵役的特权；这一特权于1911年3月17日被取消。征召令下达后多地发生反抗，大批壮丁外逃，据意大利领事馆人员称，仅的黎波里周边就有不少于1万名青壮年前往法属突尼斯。

sources.title: Italy's War for a Desert（Francis McCullagh，1912，Internet Archive 全文）
sources.quote: Ever since the Revolution in Turkey, the Arabs and the Jews of Libya have jealously guarded their exemption from serving in the Turkish Army, but this privilege was annulled on March 17, 1911. When the conscripts were called up, there were many outbreaks of rebellion. ... the writer was assured by Signor Saman, of the Italian Consulate, that not less than ten thousand of the sturdiest young Arabs had left the country around Tripoli and gone over into French territory.

fact: 意大利为这场战争的开支远超预算：开战之初估计每月3000万里拉足够，实际达到每月8000万里拉，且持续时间远长于预估。关于战争总费用，两种记述相差悬殊——一种称共耗费约13亿里拉，比焦利蒂战前估计多出近10亿；另一种称约5.27亿里拉。

sources.title: Giovanni Giolitti（Wikiwand，转述 Giolitti 传记材料）
sources.quote: Instead of the 30 million lire a month judged sufficient at its beginning, it reached a cost of 80 million a month for a much longer period than was originally estimated. The war cost Italy 1.3 billion lire, nearly a billion more than Giolitti estimated before the war. This ruined ten years of fiscal prudence.

sources.title: Turco-Italian War (1911-1912)（WarHistory.org）
sources.quote: More Italian soldiers died of disease than enemy bullets – 1,948 to 1,432 – but what many of them were calling a "war for a desert" by the end of the conflict had cost Italy around 527 million lire and had drawn off a large portion of its army and modern military equipment.

fact: 罗马银行（Banco di Roma）自1907年前后在利比亚大量购入可耕地，尤其集中在昔兰尼加，购价高昂；1911年初因对意大利是否出兵产生怀疑，该行昔兰尼加土地中很大一部分以每单位10里拉买入、却只能按2里拉的贱价卖出。意大利的占领使该行免于灾难，战争期间政府工程、木筏、桥梁、牲畜、粮食、军营等合同大多落入该行及其代理人手中。

sources.title: Italy's War for a Desert（Francis McCullagh，1912，Internet Archive 全文）
sources.quote: At the beginning of the year 1911, when serious doubts were entertained off the conquest ever coming off, a large portion of the Bank's Cyrenaica land, bought at 10 lire, was sold at the ridiculous price of 2 lire. The loss, of course, was heavy. The occupation saved the Bank from a disaster which could not have been otherwise delayed, and since it has in its possession nearly all the reclaimable land in Tripoli it is evident that its gains will be colossal ... They supplied the rafts and bridges used for the disembarkation of the troops, the animals, the food, the war material.

fact: 意大利占领后于1913年设立土地局（Ufficio Fondiario），任务是厘清地权并把无主地收归公产，以供未来殖民安置。土地局最初假定未耕地属于私有、须经证明方可入公产，因此工作十年之后，公产仅3600公顷；1922年7月18日沃尔皮总督颁布敕令，改假定未耕地为无主，才使公产迅速扩张。到1933年，的黎波里塔尼亚有50万英亩纳入公产，其中25万英亩集中在仅378名租让者手中。

sources.title: The Italian Colonization of Libya: 1911 to 1940（Youngstown State University 学位论文，Aliberti）
sources.quote: After the Italians took over, the Italian Land Office was set up in 1913 with the mission of determining land ownership and accumulating unowned land into a public domain that could be used for future colonial settlements. ... Consequently, after ten years of work, only 3600 hectares (approximately 8895 acres) of land was in the public domain. ... By 1933, the colonial government reported that 500,000 acres had been incorporated under the public domain in Tripolitania. Of this total, 250,000 acres were in the hands of only 378 settlers.
